exercise.name: 123 Back Drill
aliases: Triangle cone drill: sprint, shuffle, backpedal

reference.title: 123 Back Drill (male)
reference.note: Used only to identify the movement. Cone order and footwork confirmed from a Physitrack clinical exercise and a JMU strength and conditioning manual. This rig, artwork and animation are original.

exercise.laterality: Alternating limbs. Run both directions: the right side is anticlockwise (sprint to the front-right cone first); the left side mirrors it to clockwise.

muscleNotes.quads_r: Main braking muscle: the right quadriceps works hardest on the final plant at cone 3 (eccentric knee-extensor strength is linked to deceleration ability; Harper 2022).
muscleNotes.quads_l: Brakes on the penultimate step into cone 3 and on the outside plant at cone 2 before the backpedal.
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Hip extension for the sprint push-off and in the low braking position (clinical opinion; no drill-specific EMG found).
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Hip extension for the sprint push-off and in the low braking position (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Hip abductor: the right (trail) leg drives the shuffle to the left (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Hip abductor: the left (lead) leg catches each shuffle step and keeps the knee over the foot (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.adductors_r: Pull the trail leg in behind the lead leg in the shuffle (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.adductors_l: Control the wide base in the shuffle and on the outside plant at cone 2 (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.calves_r: Push off the balls of the feet in all three segments (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.calves_l: Push off the balls of the feet in all three segments (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Hip extension in the sprint; mostly isometric during braking (Harper 2022).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Hip extension in the sprint; mostly isometric during braking (Harper 2022).
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_r: Drive the knee forward in the sprint steps (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_l: Drive the knee forward in the sprint steps (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.core: Holds the trunk stacked over the hips through braking and direction changes (McBurnie 2021).
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Resist sideways trunk lean on the plants, a recognised COD risk factor (McBurnie 2021).
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Resist sideways trunk lean on the plants (McBurnie 2021).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Keep the chest up in the forward lean and the low backpedal posture.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Keep the chest up in the forward lean and the low backpedal posture.

breathing.pattern: Breathe naturally and rhythmically through each lap; do not hold the breath on the plants. Recover with slow, relaxed breathing between laps.
breathing.cadence: Natural; no fixed count (no study on breathing in agility drills was found)

prescription.work: One lap takes roughly 5-10 s at 5 yd sides (estimate by analogy with the T-test)
prescription.reps: 4-8 laps per set, half anticlockwise and half clockwise
prescription.rest: About 20-40 s between laps and 2-3 min between sets
prescription.intensity: Start at walking or jog pace; full speed only once technique is clean
prescription.frequency: 1-3 times per week, early in the session after a warm-up
prescription.progression: Walk-through, then jog, then full speed; then reactive versions where a partner calls the next cone

cues.text: Start in an athletic stance at cone 1, facing the gap between cones 2 and 3: soft knees, weight on the balls of your feet.
Drive out low toward cone 3 and push the ground back; arms pump.
Chop your feet to slow down: several short steps, hips sink, before you reach the cone.
Knee over toes on every plant; don't let it cave in.
Shuffle to cone 2 with hips and chest facing forward; feet never cross or click.
Backpedal low and light back to cone 1: shoulders over your toes, short quick steps.
Stay low at every cone; don't stand up between segments.

mistakes.mistake: Braking in one big last step (straight-legged plant)
mistakes.fix: Start slowing earlier with 2-3 short steps; sink the hips on the penultimate step.

mistakes.mistake: Knee caving inward on the plant
mistakes.fix: Slow down and plant with the knee over the second toe; widen the base slightly.
Keep the hips low through each change of direction.

mistakes.mistake: Crossing the feet or turning the hips during the shuffle
mistakes.fix: Push off the trail leg, feet stay apart, chest stays forward.

mistakes.mistake: Leaning back or sitting on the heels during the backpedal
mistakes.fix: Shoulders over the toes, weight on the balls of the feet, short steps.

mistakes.mistake: Turning to run back to cone 1 instead of backpedalling
mistakes.fix: Face the front cones for the whole lap; only the direction of travel changes.

mistakes.mistake: Excess sideways trunk lean on the plants
mistakes.fix: Keep the trunk stacked over the hips; lower the speed until control returns.
Alternate anticlockwise and clockwise laps so both legs brake.

kinematics.norm: Up to about 100° on the penultimate braking step; lower the centre of mass with hip, knee and ankle flexion
No drill-specific data; short, quick steps at drill pace
About 45° in early acceleration of a full sprint start (coaching article); less over a short, drill-pace start. Trunk slightly back when braking.

kinematics.peak: No turn for the whole lap
kinematics.norm: Hips and chest face forward in the shuffle (T-test rule); forward, sideways and backward travel only

kinematics.setup: Front cones 183 cm apart; cone 1 183 cm behind their midpoint (40% scale)
kinematics.peak: Pelvis path: sprint 141 cm, shuffle 115 cm, backpedal 141 cm
kinematics.norm: About 5 yd (4.57 m) spacing by convention; shorter (3 m) for beginners or small spaces

cautions: Knee injury or ACL history: non-contact ACL injuries are linked to deceleration and direction changes, especially on the final plant. Reduce speed and turn sharpness first and follow a clinician's return-to-sport plan.
Balance problems, older adults or pregnancy: backpedalling raises fall risk. A spotter behind the backpedal finish can help.
Stop if you feel sharp joint pain, the knee gives way, or form breaks down (steps lose rhythm, torso rocks back).
Use a dry, non-slip surface and supportive court or field shoes.
modify: Patellofemoral (front-of-knee) pain: backward running loaded the kneecap less than forward running in one study of 20 runners, so the backpedal may be tolerated better than the braking-heavy sprint; slow the sprint and brake over more steps.
Ankle sprain history: jog pace and shorter sides first; build ankle and calf strength.
Need enough eccentric leg strength to tolerate braking forces before running at full speed.
regressions: Walk-through of the pattern, then jog pace.
No backpedal: turn and walk back to cone 1.
progressions: Full speed once every plant is controlled.
Reactive version: a partner calls the next cone or 'back' (two or three choices).
Alternate anticlockwise and clockwise laps within a set.
